subject: Help improving documentation of related functions:

messages.author: 638920adbe92dd8a
messages.subject: Help improving documentation of related functions:
parts:
Dear all,

in one of my packages I have two functions fun_a and fun_b defined in a way similar to this:

#' @rdname fun
#'
#' @name fun_a
#'
#' @title function A
#'
#' @description what function A does
#'
#' @param x variable required in input
#'
#' @export
#'
fun_a <- function(x, ...){
    --- code
    return(res)
}

#' @rdname fun
#'
#' @name fun_b
#'
#' @title function b
#'
#' @description what function A does
#'
#' @export
fun_b <- function(...){
    res <- fun_a(...)
    -- manipulate a bit res
    -- return the modified result.
    return(res)
}

When I run document(), 
the Usage section appears like

fun_a( x, ...)

fun_b(...)

I would like to override the Usage of fun_b to be
fun_b(x,...).

Is this possible? How can I do this?

Thanks a lot in advance to all of you for the help, 

Cheers,
Luca

messages.author: 638920adbe92dd8a
messages.subject: [SOLVED] Re: Help improving documentation of related functions:
parts:
Sorry, for the spam I finally found out how to do it.

When I opened RStudio, I was exposed to a nice @usage roclet that does the trick.

In the specific example one has to add:

@usage fun_b(x,...)

While this does the trick, I was wondering, is there some more elegant way have exactly the formals defined in fun_a? this way if I change the syntax for fun_a I have to remember to copy and paste it into @usage in fun_b, which I 
would prefer to avoid.

Cheers,
Luca
